turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (DOCTOR): Come through, have a seat. What can I do for you today?
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Honestly, it's hardly anything. I nearly didn't come. The knee's been a bit off, that's all.
[SEG0003] person_1 (DOCTOR): Alright, tell me how it's been for you.

[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Right knee. Going down the stairs it grumbles, and at night if I turn over it wakes me sometimes. Months, maybe since the spring, I couldn't tell you exactly. Not every day, and I still get about fine.
[SEG0005] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it stop you doing things, or are you mostly carrying on?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Carrying on. I'm not an invalid. Stairs are just annoying, that's it.
[SEG0007] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any swelling you've spotted, or does the knee give way under you?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): No swelling. And it doesn't give way. I'm not keeling over.
[SEG0009] person_1 (DOCTOR): Does it lock, get stuck at all?
[SEG0010] person_2 (PATIENT): No, nothing like that.
[SEG0011] person_1 (DOCTOR): What have you tried for it so far?
[SEG0012] person_2 (PATIENT): That gel from the chemist. Diclofenac. I rub a bit on the knee.
[SEG0013] person_1 (DOCTOR): How often?
[SEG0014] person_2 (PATIENT): Twice a day. Morning and when I get into bed. Takes the edge off, I suppose. Not a miracle.
[SEG0015] person_1 (DOCTOR): Any tablets as well, or just the gel?
[SEG0016] person_2 (PATIENT): Sometimes the, um, naproxen— no, I don't take naproxen. Ibuprofen, from the pharmacy, if it's a bad day. I'm not one for pills.
[SEG0017] person_1 (DOCTOR): Do you know the strength, and how many you take?
[SEG0018] person_2 (PATIENT): Two hundred milligram ones. One or two, with a bit of food. Maybe two or three times in a week. Not regularly.
[SEG0019] person_1 (DOCTOR): And your stomach, with those? Any pain, sickness, that sort of thing?
[SEG0020] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Stomach's completely fine. No trouble at all.
[SEG0021] person_1 (DOCTOR): Okay. Has your weight shifted at all lately? Knees notice that, sometimes.
[SEG0022] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, yeah. Half a stone, maybe, since Christmas. People go on about it. I'm not huge.
[SEG0023] person_1 (DOCTOR): Are you managing any walks, or has that dropped off?
[SEG0024] person_2 (PATIENT): I walk to the paper shop and back. That's plenty. Gyms are not for me.
[SEG0025] person_1 (DOCTOR): Mind if I have a look and a feel of the knee?
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Go on, then. You'll see it's nothing.
[SEG0027] person_1 (DOCTOR): There's tenderness along the inside of the right knee, and a little crunching as I bend it. No swelling that I can feel.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): There you are. I said it wasn't swollen.
[SEG0029] person_1 (DOCTOR): Did you see any of the cricket over the weekend? Absolute chaos at the end.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Had the radio on while I was peeling potatoes. England were all over the shop. Typical.
[SEG0031] person_1 (DOCTOR): My grandson was yelling at the telly. Eight years old and he's already picking the team.
[SEG0032] person_2 (PATIENT): Ha. Mine's mad for football. They came round Sunday and the ball ended up in the flower bed twice.
[SEG0033] person_1 (DOCTOR): The weather didn't help, pouring from lunchtime. I sat in traffic on the ring road forty minutes just for a pint of milk.
[SEG0034] person_2 (PATIENT): Those roadworks by the big supermarket. Been there since March. You'd think they'd finished by now.
[SEG0035] person_1 (DOCTOR): I know. Anyway, sorry, back to you, if that's alright.
[SEG0036] person_2 (PATIENT): Oh, one thing. I said the stomach was fine. Well, I do get a bit of heartburn after the ibuprofen. Not every time. It's minor, not proper pain. Hardly worth mentioning.
[SEG0037] person_1 (DOCTOR): I'm glad you said. Keep the ibuprofen just for the odd bad day, and if that heartburn gets worse, leave the tablets off. The gel is easier on the stomach.
[SEG0038] person_2 (PATIENT): The gel's fine. I'll carry on with that. The tablets are only now and then anyway.

[SEG0039] person_1 (DOCTOR): From what you've told me, and from examining it, I think this is most likely wear and tear, osteoarthritis in the right knee. That's my working impression, not a definite diagnosis.
[SEG0040] person_2 (PATIENT): Wear and tear. I'm seventy-four. Course it is. Everyone my age has something.
[SEG0041] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might refer you to physiotherapy, or later on we could think about an injection into the knee, but I don't want us to decide either of those today.
[SEG0042] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't fancy a needle, thanks. And physio sounds like a lot of faff for a niggle.
[SEG0043] person_1 (DOCTOR): That's fair. We'll leave both for now.
[SEG0044] person_2 (PATIENT): Good.
[SEG0045] person_1 (DOCTOR): We might do an x-ray if it hasn't settled. Otherwise I won't put you through it yet.
[SEG0046] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't need a scan. It'll sort itself.
[SEG0047] person_1 (DOCTOR): Let's see you in two weeks, and we'll take another look then.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): Two weeks, alright. I'll be fine, you'll see. Probably a waste of your time.
